items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: we had a good group in Chicago called the MJT + 3, young people. Frank Strozier, Bob Cranshaw, Walter Perkins, myself, Bobby Bryant, you know.

ctx.x: Yeah, you’ve got to go because you go to play, say in Chicago, you’ve got to know when to make your move. After you say well we’ve done everything we can do here, it’s time to make the move to the Big Apple. Now see New York City, you never make the move because you’re never not there because there’s things to be done, even now, I mean just the city itself. But no matter what town you’re in, you can be in L.A. or Memphis or Chattanooga, whatever. There comes a time when you say, well we’ve gone as far as we

can go because we had a good group in Chicago called the MJT + 3, young people. Frank Strozier, Bob Cranshaw, Walter Perkins, myself, Bobby Bryant, you know. And we were very successful during that time. There were three groups that had hit records: Ahmad Jamal Trio, Ramsey Lewis Trio, and our group, you know. But after the work kind of subsided we said okay, it’s time to make the move to New York, which is what we did, because when we went to New York we had work lined up. We didn’t go there just to be checking…
